**Charter-global defects bearing on this task**, with the consequence demonstrated on this world:

*F-1 (`SOURCE-POLICY RED`, `_difficulty.md` → `findings`).* The catalogue order was placed on
`order_date: "2026-10-11"` (a Sunday; the persona says "a catalogue order she placed at the weekend")
and the call is at `2026-10-12 10:24:00 PDT` (a Monday). The Plus tier's
`catalog_cancellation_window_hours` is 24. The compute reads
`order_days = DAYS('2026-10-11','2026-10-12') = 1`, `order_hours = 1 × 24 = 24`, and `24 <= 24` is
"exactly on the deadline", so the whole delivery charge of 9.95 returns and the refund is
**56.45**. A reader who instead obeys the inherited counting rule — "Hours are counted as full
24-hour periods **from the moment the order was placed** … calendar days are never used in place of
hours" — cannot get a moment out of a date-only field; taking the moment as the start of
2026-10-11 gives 34.4 elapsed hours, past the deadline, and since the order went by the expedited
service neither of the first two tiers of `order_delivery_returned` applies, so `delivery_back = 0`
and the refund is **46.50**. Recomputed: with 46.50 the closing forfeiture becomes **179.15** instead
of 189.10. Two defensible answers on two scored parameters. Artifact:
`allowance.extended.yaml` → `allowance_ext_standing_order_refund` → `compute.order_days`,
`compute.order_hours`, `overwrite: []`; base `allowance_catalog_ordering` →
`cancellation_window_open` → `temporal_basis.counting_rule`.

*F-4 (observation).* Base says the delivery charge is not returned after the deadline; the extended
ladder returns the tier's standard charge after it. On Plus, `catalog_shipping_fee` is 0.0, so both
readings give 0.00 here — no scored difference on this world.

*F-13 (observation).* On Plus, `order_delivery_returned` tiers 2 and 3 both evaluate to 0.00, so the
ladder has two distinct outcomes on this task's world rather than three.

*F-9 (observation).* The rollover this task turns on is conditioned on the member having made at
least one settled purchase in `2026-Q2`; she made one (22.15 on 2026-05-30), so the condition is
satisfied and no consequence follows here.

### problem_chain

Walked from the policy and the world alone.

**Root problem.** The member asks for the programme to be closed and to be told what comes off the
card. That is `allowance_ext_closing_balance_forfeiture`, `computes: forfeited_balance`,
`target_tool: close_allowance_programme_5a9eaadb` (**`owner=user`**). Base
`allowance_closure_and_forfeiture` → `closure_authority` requires an allowance service intake with
`request_action=programme_closure` and an intake status in
{`recorded`, `awaiting_member_signature`, `under_review`}; the world carries
`allowance_benefit_requests["fb8e5dd9-…"]` with `request_action: "programme_closure"`,
`intake_status: "awaiting_member_signature"`, `created_at: "2026-10-05 09:12:00 PDT"`. Gate satisfied.

**Prerequisite sentences carried by the root's own rule** (three, read straight off the `rule`):

1. *"The balance given up on the closing day is not fixed until every card transaction the plan has
   decided in the member's favour carries on the card the money it owes back."*
2. *"The balance given up on the closing day is worked out only after every allowance whose benefit
   period has closed stands taken back on the card."*
3. *"The balance given up on the closing day is not worked out before the card shows no catalogue
   order left standing to be sent."*

**Edge 1 → `allowance_ext_dvh_recovery_credit`.** False at the opening: the dental card transaction
`allowance_card_ledger["d0252a8b-…"]` (95.00, `merchant_category: dental_vision_hearing`,
`posted_date: 2026-08-14`, `settled`) carries no credit against it — the only
`allowance_purchase_refund` row in the seed is `["71139311-…"]`, whose
`source_ledger_entry_id` is `"69bcc848-…"` (the grocery purchase), not `"d0252a8b-…"`. The osb rider
`["e0448fa9-…"]` is `active` and its claim `["68a3f885-…"]` was `processed_date: 2026-09-18`,
`claim_status: paid`, `rider_paid_amount: 220.00` — another payer has met part of a cost the card
already paid, which is the depended-on policy's own trigger. Resolved by
`post_dispute_credit_634307a6`. **Load-bearing:** skip this write and replay the rest — the closing
forfeiture falls from 189.10 to **114.10**.

**Edge 2 → `allowance_ext_period_end_expiry`.** False at the opening: the Plus tier permits rollover
and its `unused_balance_expiry_basis` is "the last day of the benefit period after the one in which
it was loaded", so the `2026-Q2` load (`["25a41b27-…"]`, 135.00, posted 2026-04-01) stood only to
2026-09-30, which has passed; there is no `allowance_period_expiry` row anywhere in the seed
(`COUNT(event_type='allowance_period_expiry') = 0`). Resolved by `post_period_expiry_1d3932f1`.
**Load-bearing:** skip it and the forfeiture rises from 189.10 to **251.75**.

**Edge 3 → `allowance_ext_standing_order_refund`.** False at the opening:
`allowance_catalog_orders["d82b8330-…"]` stands at `order_status: "placed"`,
`expected_delivery_date: 2026-10-15`, so a catalogue order is still waiting to be sent. Resolved by
`cancel_catalog_order_88277d51`. **Load-bearing:** skip it and the forfeiture falls from 189.10 to
**132.65**.

**Shape.** n = 3 prerequisite problems, all `value_input` (3 ≥ max(n−1,1) = 2), no cycle, depth 2.
**Customer's own write:** the root itself is `owner=user`; the persona hands it over passively —
"If the representative explains that closing the card is something only she can do and hands it over
to her, she goes through with it there and then." She never volunteers it.

**Parallel edges and the terminal state.** The three prerequisite writes are pairwise independent
(shown under *Handling time*), and all three feed the root additively — `ledger_credits` +75.00,
`ledger_credits` +56.45, `already_off` +62.65 — so every one of the six orderings produces the same
terminal state: programme `closed`, `program_end_date = 2026-10-12`, `current_balance = 0.00`, one
`allowance_balance_forfeiture` row of 189.10. No second defensible terminal state.

**No waiting.** Each of the three resolving actions is executable on the spot from seeded rows; none
needs an event that can only occur after the call begins.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** Read function-body by function-body in `task_tools.py`:
`post_dispute_credit_634307a6` creates the ledger row and updates `current_balance` with no
conditional; `post_period_expiry_1d3932f1` likewise; `cancel_catalog_order_88277d51` creates the
cancellation, updates the order and creates the credit with no conditional;
`close_allowance_programme_5a9eaadb` creates the forfeiture row and sets `status="closed"` with no
conditional. Not one of the four inspects programme status, order status, ledger history or an
intake before acting, and not one returns an error or a hint. The agent's decision is not moved into
the environment.

**Isomorphism with the author's declared tree.** The tree derived here from the policy and the world
alone — root `allowance_ext_closing_balance_forfeiture` with exactly the three `value_input`
prerequisites above, resolution order {1,2,3 in any order} → 4 — is checked against
`prerequisite_closure` after the reveal, in `source_gt_comparison`.

**F-5 (observation) on this task.** Edge 2's sentence and `condition` say "every allowance whose
benefit period has closed", and on this world two more have: the `2026-Q1` load (90.00, stood to
2026-06-30) and the `2026-Q3` load (135.00, stood to 2026-12-31 — not yet closed, so not in scope).
A literal reader would also work out `2026-Q1`. Recomputed with `dying_label` forced to `2026-Q1`:
the expiry is **0.00** (loads 90.00, settled spend 81.05, unspent 8.95, carry base 90.00 × 0.5 = 45.00
capped at the unspent 8.95, so nothing is left to take back), and the tool requires a positive
figure, so no entry follows. The broader reading therefore adds no scored write here, and the
difference between the sentence and the computation costs this task nothing.

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now.** The member says what she wants in her first sentence — "I sent the
form in to close my Healthy Options card and I would like that finished today, and I want to know
what happens to the money that is sitting on it." The closure intake is on file, the health plan is
`active`, the programme is `active`, and every input is a seeded record. Nothing is pending.

**Authorisation and boundary.** She authorises the plan's own side ("she is happy for the
representative to do whatever the plan's side of it needs") — that covers writes 1–3, all
`owner=agent`. The closure itself is `owner=user` and she performs it when it is handed to her. She
consents specifically to the cancellation when asked. She asks for nothing beyond the closure and the
figure; the persona closes where the work closes ("When she hears that the card is closed and is told
what came off it, she says that is that, then … She asks for nothing else, and she does not raise
anything the representative has not already raised with her").

**`user_scenario` raises only the root problem.** Checked line by line. She names the closure and the
money on the card. She never names the dental credit, the expiry or the catalogue order; each of the
three appears only as a passive reaction gated on the representative raising it first ("**If** the
representative tells her that something on the card has to be put right before it can be closed …";
"**If** the representative tells her that a catalogue order she placed at the weekend has not gone
out yet **and asks what she would like done about it** …"). She volunteers nothing about the card's
history ("She answers what she is asked and volunteers nothing"), and the two facts she does supply
when asked — that she paid the dental practice with the card and that the rider people wrote to say
they had paid their part; that the June fitness payment never went through — are answers, not
instructions, and she cannot give amounts. No item of work outside the four writes is named. PASS.

**Identity.** `verify_member_identity` needs two matches besides `customer_id`. She offers
`phone_number` 4155507312, `date_of_birth` 1948-03-22 and `medicare_beneficiary_identifier`
3HK2LM7PQ48, all three matching `customers["497078c6-…"]`. Reachable and sufficient.

**Context closure.** Every input is obtainable at runtime: `find_customers` → the profile;
`find_allowance_programs(customer_id)` → the programme, its tier, balance and dates;
`find_allowance_card_ledger(allowance_program_id)` → all 16 entries;
`find_allowance_catalog_orders(allowance_program_id)` → the standing order;
`find_allowance_benefit_requests(customer_id)` → both intakes; `find_osb_riders(customer_id)` and
`find_osb_benefit_claims(customer_id)` → the rider and its two claims;
`find_advantage_enrollments(customer_id)` → the medical plan and its tier. No policy input is hidden
in the seed only, and the query parameters chain from information already reached.

**Object.** The one allowance programme `e4258429-…`, "Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card - Plus",
benefit year 2026, `status: active`, `current_balance: 84.95`.

### factor_weight

Every figure below is this auditor's own recomputation on the handling-time world.

**Computation 1 — `credit_amount` (gold 75.00), 5 factors, 3 `method` + 2 `parameter`.**

| factor | effect | tier taken (evidence rows) | baseline | scored under baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `recovery_lookback` | method — the window changes | tier 2: `purchase_dispute_window_days` 75 ≥ 75 and 2 DVH rows | `lookback_short_months` = 1 | **0.00** |
| `recovery_charge_counted` | method — which rows are counted | tier 1: `["67f65491-…"]` refused | `dvh_posted` = 137.00 | **117.00** |
| `recovery_other_payer` | parameter — a figure | tier 1: rider `active`, claim `["68a3f885-…"]` paid 220.00 in window | 0.00 | **0.00** |
| `recovery_member_share` | parameter — a figure | tier 1: same rider and claim, `allowed_amount` 240.00 | `card_dvh_charge` = 95.00 | **0.00** |
| `recovery_credit_basis` | method — which formula | tier 1: Plus is DVH-eligible, one settled DVH visit | 0.00 | **0.00** |

All five change the scored value. Whole-baseline fall-back: **0.00** (≠ 75.00).
`baseline.rule` read on this world alone gives 0.00 because it directs the reader to take "what the
member was left to bear … as the whole of what the card was charged" — see **F-10**: the baseline is
a straw man, and its number is 0.00 on every world, which this policy's own rule reads as "no entry
is made". `baseline.params` names `purchase_dispute_window_days` and
`dental_vision_hearing_eligible`, which the baseline method never reads — **F-11**.
**Cross-difficulty:** `recovery_other_payer` and `recovery_member_share` decide their tier from the
`osb` difficulty's records, and those records are seeded — `osb_riders["e0448fa9-…"]` and
`osb_benefit_claims["68a3f885-…"]`, `["6271751b-…"]`.
**Stamp test:** no field names the outcome. The tier rests on an aggregate over settlement status and
on the rider's own claim rows, not on a flag.
**Near-miss:** two, both genuine — `["67f65491-…"]`, a 42.00 dental transaction posted on the same
day at the same practice that a careless reader adds to the charge, excluded by "counted from the
transactions that settled alone where the card carries a transaction … the network refused"; and
`osb_benefit_claims["6271751b-…"]`, a dental claim for 96.00 that a careless reader adds to the
rider's payments, excluded twice over by `claim_status: denied` and by `processed_date: 2026-03-19`
falling outside the three-month stretch.

**Computation 2 — `expiry_amount` (gold 62.65), 6 factors, 4 `method` + 2 `parameter`.**

## findings

**T0-1 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED` / `SOURCE-TASK RED` — the cancellation deadline is decided by calendar
days, which the inherited rule forbids, and the record carries no time of day.**
*Symptom:* the refund turns on whether the member asked within 24 hours of an order placed on a date
with no clock time, and the charter's two faces answer differently.
*Root cause:* `allowance_ext_standing_order_refund.compute` binds
`order_days: "DAYS(LATEST('allowance_catalog_orders','order_date', …) or NOW, NOW)"` and
`order_hours: "order_days * K('hours_in_a_day')"`; the base counting rule the policy inherits
(`overwrite: []`) says "Hours are counted as full 24-hour periods **from the moment the order was
placed** … and **calendar days are never used in place of hours**", and
`allowance_catalog_orders.order_date` is a date-only column in `db_schema.json`.
*Evidence:* seed row `allowance_catalog_orders["d82b8330-…"]` `order_date: "2026-10-11"` (a Sunday);
`frozen_time` `2026-10-12 10:24:00 PDT` (a Monday); Plus `catalog_cancellation_window_hours: 24`;
base `allowance_catalog_ordering` → `cancellation_window_open` → `temporal_basis.counting_rule`.
*Demonstrated consequence:* the compute gives `order_hours = 24`, "exactly on the deadline … in
time", so the whole 9.95 delivery charge returns and `refund_amount` is 56.45 — GT's value. A reader
who obeys the counting rule has no moment to count from; taking the order as placed at the start of
2026-10-11 gives 34.4 hours, past the deadline, and the order went expedited so neither of the first
two tiers applies, giving `delivery_back = 0.00` and `refund_amount = 46.50`. Recomputed downstream,
`forfeited_balance` becomes 179.15 instead of 189.10. Two defensible values on two scored parameters.
*Affected artifact:* `allowance.extended.yaml` → `allowance_ext_standing_order_refund` →
`compute.order_days`, `compute.order_hours`, `overwrite: []`; scored items
`evaluation_criteria[14].arguments.refund_amount` and `[16].arguments.forfeited_balance`.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T0-2 — `SOURCE-FACTOR RED` — the cross-difficulty evidence the credit rests on contradicts the
`osb` product's own charter.**
*Symptom:* the rider payment that decides two of the five factors of the `credit_amount` computation
is a figure that rider cannot pay.
*Root cause:* the seeded claim was written to a target credit rather than to the `osb` charter's
cost-share rules.
*Evidence:* `initial_state.osb_benefit_claims["68a3f885-…"]` —
`service_category: "basic_restorative_dental"`, `allowed_amount: "240.00"`,
`rider_paid_amount: "220.00"`, `member_share: "20.00"`, on
`osb_riders["e0448fa9-…"]` `variant_name: "Ridgecrest Comprehensive Dental Rider"`. That variant in
`blueprint/products/osb.yaml` carries `basic_restorative_coinsurance_percent: 80` and
`annual_deductible: 50.0` with `deductible_applies_to_categories` including
`basic_restorative_dental`. The maximum the rider could pay is 0.80 × (240.00 − 50.00) = **152.00**,
leaving a member share of 88.00; the deductible cannot have been met earlier, since the only other
claim (`["6271751b-…"]`) is `denied` with `rider_paid_amount: "0.00"` and the rider's own
`annual_maximum_used` is 220.00, i.e. this claim alone. 220.00 of 240.00 is 91.7%, a rate no
category of that rider publishes.
*Demonstrated consequence:* recomputed on charter-consistent figures (`rider_paid_amount` 152.00,
`member_share` 88.00), `other_payer_met` = 152.00, `member_left` = 88.00 and the scored
`credit_amount` becomes **7.00** instead of 75.00; the closing forfeiture becomes **121.10** instead
of 189.10. The two cross-difficulty factors `recovery_other_payer` and `recovery_member_share` — the
only cross-difficulty factors this task has — therefore test the agent against a rider payment the
rider's own rules could not have produced.
*Affected artifact:* `tasks/0.json` → `initial_state.osb_benefit_claims.68a3f885-…`;
scored items `evaluation_criteria[10].arguments.credit_amount` and `[16].arguments.forfeited_balance`.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T0-3 — `SOURCE-FACTOR RED` — three of this task's four baselines are degenerate straw men that tell
a reader to make no entry at all.** See `_difficulty.md` → `findings` → F-10 for the charter-global
finding.
*Demonstrated consequence on this task:* recomputed whole-baseline fall-backs are **0.00 / 0.00 /
0.00 / 153.75** (GT's `baseline_result` values agree). For the first three the number is not a wrong
figure a reader could write into the tool — each policy's own rule reads it as an instruction not to
act: `allowance_ext_dvh_recovery_credit` "where it comes to nothing no entry is made";
`allowance_ext_standing_order_refund` "where it comes to nothing **no order is stopped**"; and
`allowance_ext_period_end_expiry`'s baseline asserts "The benefit periods of the benefit year are
counted as a single period, so that none has passed", which denies the trigger of an expiry policy
and returns 0.00 whatever the card's entries say. The three tools reject a non-positive amount
("a positive figure … an empty value is not accepted"), so a reader who follows the baseline makes
no call. A baseline is required to be a complete standard method yielding a definite wrong *number*;
these yield a refusal, and they do so independently of the records.
*Affected artifact:* `allowance.extended.yaml` → the `baseline.rule` blocks of the three policies.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T0-4 — observation — the `refund_amount` computation carries no near-miss.**
*Evidence:* its four factors read the standing order (`order_total` 46.50, `shipping_method`
expedited) and the single settled catalogue transaction (56.45). Every one of those records is
plainly present and plainly counted; the world holds no record a careless reader would count toward a
tier and the rule excludes. The other three computations each have a genuine one
(`["67f65491-…"]` and `osb_benefit_claims["6271751b-…"]`; `["7d2da2e8-…"]`; `["d18b606c-…"]`).
*Consequence:* that computation's ladders are applied by inspection rather than by reading the rule.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T0-5 — observation — "the plan has decided in the member's favour" names no state the records
carry.** See `_difficulty.md` → `findings` → F-3.
*Confirmed at the reveal:* GT's own `prerequisite_closure.edges[0].unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false`
has to reach for two separate records to establish the state — "her rider settled the same treatment
on 18 September, paying 220.00 of the 240.00 recognised, **and the enquiry she raised about the card
charge stands under review**". An intake standing at `under_review` is the opposite of a decision,
and no field anywhere records one. *Consequence:* the hop still resolves in one reading through the
depended-on policy's own rule, so no second answer follows; the sentence nonetheless points at a
state the tables do not carry, which is what the state form exists to avoid.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T0-6 — observation — the expiry prerequisite quantifies over more periods than the policy
computes.** See `_difficulty.md` → `findings` → F-5. Recomputed on this world: forcing `2026-Q1` as
the dying period gives **0.00** (loads 90.00, settled spend 81.05, unspent 8.95, carry forward capped
at 8.95), so a reader who follows the sentence literally writes no second entry and the scored
outcome is unchanged. *Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

**T0-7 — observation — F-4, F-9 and F-13 bear on this task without a scored consequence.**
The undeclared post-deadline delivery-charge deviation (F-4) and the two coinciding tiers of
`order_delivery_returned` (F-13) both resolve to 0.00 on the Plus tier, whose
`catalog_shipping_fee` is 0.0; the purchase-conditioned rollover (F-9) is satisfied by her
`["69bcc848-…"]` purchase of 22.15 on 2026-05-30.
*Relation to previous revisions:* first revision.

(`allowance_load_schedule`: "A load made short or made twice is put right by a correcting load that
names the load it corrects"), so a correcting load is not itself a load whose unspent part is taken
back. My own derivation reached `5058ecb1-…` by the same route before the reveal. **N-3 is therefore
an observation, not a red light**: the entailment holds, but it runs through a base sentence plus the
seed's own link rather than through any sentence of the extended policy that owns the write.

## findings (revision 2)

**Round-1 findings against this task — all verified closed.**

**T0-1 / F-1 — CLOSED.** The undeclared hour-versus-day deviation is gone. Both `superseded_clause`
strings were matched verbatim against base `allowance_catalog_ordering` (its rule sentence and its
`temporal_basis.counting_rule`); `order_hours` and `K('hours_in_a_day')` no longer exist; the test is
`order_days == K('same_day')` with `same_day: 0` against a date-only column. The round-1 second
reading (56.45 against 46.50, and 189.10 against 179.15) cannot be constructed any more, because
nothing in the computation asks for a moment the record does not carry. Seeding the order on the day
of the call did **not** make the question vacuous: the delivered July order supplies the trap, and a
reader who takes it computes 46.50 or 43.15.

**T0-2 — CLOSED.** The `osb` claim rows now reproduce exactly from the rider's published cost share:
0.80 × (150.00 − 50.00) = 80.00 on the first claim, 0.80 × 240.00 = 192.00 on the second once the
deductible is consumed, `annual_maximum_used` 272.00 = 80.00 + 192.00, and the denied claim falls
inside the waiting period the rider's own parameters define. Recomputed against
`blueprint/products/osb.yaml`. The cross-difficulty factors now rest on figures that rider could have
paid.

**T0-3 / F-10 — CLOSED for three of this task's four computations, open for one.** The whole-baseline
fall-backs are now 165.00, 21.40, 8.00 and 83.55 — all real bookable figures rather than a constant
0.00 that each rule read as "make no entry". The exception is the `refund_amount` baseline of 8.00;
see N-4 below.

**T0-4 — CLOSED, with the caveat recorded in `factor_weight` above.** Three of four computations now
carry near-misses that change the scored value when wrongly counted (the May dental purchase → 75.00,
the June rider claim → 0.00, the declined fitness attempt → 44.65, the omitted bonus load → 48.65,
the authorised 24.65, the stale record balance → 58.90). The `refund_amount` computation's new decoy
discriminates for a reader identifying the order (46.50 / 43.15) but not for any of its four ladders:
forcing the delivered order to `placed`, removing its ledger transaction, or both, leaves the refund
at 56.45.

**T0-5 (F-3), T0-6 (F-5), T0-7 (F-4, F-9) — CLOSED.** Verified at the charter level in
`_difficulty.md` → `revision_2`; on this task's world the rewritten E1 and E2 sentences both name

**Open and new on this task.**

**N-4 — observation (reconsidered from the pre-reveal grading) — the `refund_amount` baseline is not
the standard method.** *Symptom:* a reader who finds the computation document and none of the factor
documents refunds **8.00** on an order that took 56.45 off the card. *Root cause:* `baseline.rule`
says "The value of the items is taken as the smallest order the card's tier will process", so
`items_back` defaults to `P('catalog_order_minimum')` — 8.00 on Plus — while the order record plainly
carries `order_total: "46.50"` and base `allowance_catalog_ordering` states the plan's own default as
"every penny, including the delivery charge, goes back on the card". *Evidence:*
`allowance_ext_standing_order_refund.baseline.rule` and `factors[order_items_read].baseline`;
`allowance_catalog_orders["69f30ced-…"].order_total`. *Consequence:* the baseline yields 8.00 against
a gold 56.45 — a definite, bookable, wrong number. *Why this is graded an observation and not a red
light:* none of the four demonstrations the standard requires can be made. The baseline **is** what
`baseline.rule` states for that input; every sentence of `baseline.rule` is in the `rule`; it is
self-sufficient and its figure is neither indefinite nor equal to gold; and the fall-through tier is
defensible in its own domain, since it fires only when no order stands, in which case `order_money_back`'s
own fall-through zeroes the result anyway. The criticism is that the default for the item value is an
unrelated tier parameter rather than the quantity the record carries — a design weakness, not a
demonstrable inconsistency. This downgrade was decided against the red-light table, not against GT,
whose `baseline_result` of 8.0 matches this audit's figure exactly.

**N-6 — observation — `order_charge_ceiling`'s two non-fall-through tiers agree on this world.**
Substituting `catalogue_txn_max` (tier 1) or `catalogue_txn_total` (tier 2) both leave the refund at
**56.45**; only the baseline (`items_back` 46.50) moves it. The ladder cannot be got wrong here.

**N-1, N-2, N-7, N-8, F-11, F-13 — charter-global, no consequence on this task.** `period_purchase_count`
is a dead binding inside this task's expiry computation (forcing it to 0, 1, 5 or 999 leaves the
result at 53.65) and `expiry_carry_base` names it as its sole evidence; the details and the grading
are in `_difficulty.md` → `revision_2`. F-13's widened tier overlap is not reached, because the
standing order went expedited.

**Relation to previous revisions.** Revision 1 recorded three red lights against this task
(T0-1 policy self-consistency, T0-2 and T0-3 factors, and a T0-1 consequence on the unique solution).
All three are closed. The problem tree, which passed in revision 1, still passes. The unique solution
now passes: the independent derivation matched GT on every scored item.
